newsitem.title: INDIA: India stock markets seen hit by political worries.
newsitem.headline: India stock markets seen hit by political worries.

text.p: Indian stock markets are expected to tumble this week on fears of political instability in the wake of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao's resignation as president of the Congress party, analysts said on Sunday.
The rupee would hold its own, but could come under pressure if the political-risk factor increased in the longer term, they said.

The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index was likely to fall 100-150 points as players unwound their long positions after Rao gave up the party leadership amid a welter of corruption charges, dealers said.
"For the market this means uncertainties," said one dealer at a European brokerage firm. "Prices will weaken."

The index ended last week 0.59 points lower at 3,346.78. But the rupee was expected to stay steady with the Indian forex market dominated by a large state-owned bank, dealers said. The rupee closed at 35.71/72 to the dollar on Friday.
Bankers said they saw no immediate threat to the rupee but feared it might buckle under the pressure of lengthy political instability.
"If foreign investors postpone investment decisions, it will slow inflows and the rupee may weaken," K. Kannan, chairman of state-owned Bank of Baroda, said.
Rao quit on Saturday after a New Delhi court ordered him to appear as a co-accused in a cheating case.
Congress party support is crucial for the survival of the 13-party minority coalition government led by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
The dealer at the European broking firm said foreign investors would have to rethink the "political risk" because of the possibility of a leadership crisis in the Congress leading to a split.
"We will have to wait and see who succeeds Rao," Kannan said. "That will determine whether the party will hold together or break up into a number of factions."
The Congress Working Committee, the party's top decision-making body, meets on Monday to elect a new leader.
Traders said fresh political worries, at a time when the economy was showing signs of a slowdown and corporate earnings were being squeezed, would make the markets skittish.
Analysts said the uncertainty could affect the $400 million global depositary receipt (GDR) issue by State Bank of India (SBI) scheduled to begin roadshows this week.
But share prices would probably bounce back after the initial nervousness, some brokers said.
"The market will open nervously but will not collapse," said Jitendra Shroff, owner of broking firm V.B. Desai. "On the other hand, it could improve."

Some traders believe Rao's exit could brighten the prospects of the Congress joining the government. This would strengthen the coalition, making it less dependent on the communists for its survival, they said.
Such a government would find it easier to speed up the pace of reforms, vital to the final success of liberalisation.

"The immediate reaction will be adverse," added Ulhas Paymaster, a BSE member-broker. "But in the medium term I expect prices to rebound... We might see a stronger stable government with the Congress joining in."
